Today’s failing approach: no live build in the AI engineer interview
function
Challenge 1: Algorithm rounds miss AI engineering skills
A generic coding round asks the candidate to solve an algorithm problem. AI coding tools can solve this type of problem. The round also gives no signal on whether the candidate can build a retrieval pipeline.
Challenge 2: The design round shows no implementation
In an AI system design round, the candidate explains how a system such as a chatbot with guardrails would work. Your interviewers hear the design but do not see whether the candidate can implement any part of it.
visibility_off
Challenge 3: Take-home projects hide the build process
When a take-home process captures only the submitted code, your team cannot review how the candidate reached the result. Preparing and sending custom tasks also takes an engineer’s time.
Hire AI engineers based on a live build in Codility Interview
Your team can run the AI build and the system design discussion in one Codility Interview session. The candidate discusses the architecture on a shared whiteboard alongside the code. You can choose a Codility AI-native task or have your engineers create a custom task for the role.
Choose an AI build task for the interview
check_circle
Build AI tasks in the Codility AI-native task library make an AI system the deliverable. For example, in the Legal Document Q&A Assistant task, the candidate implements a LangChain and FAISS RAG pipeline. The pipeline answers questions about a legal document archive and returns its sources.
The DataSentinel task suits AI engineering roles closer to machine learning. In this task, the candidate builds an anomaly-detection pipeline for daily KPI readings and stores the reading history in PostgreSQL.
Your engineers can also create a multi-file task with the Codility Model Context Protocol (MCP) connector. An engineer describes the task to their own AI coding assistant, reviews the generated task and publishes it in Codility.

Questions about AI engineer interviews
An AI engineer interview is a technical interview for engineers who build applications on large language models (LLMs), such as RAG pipelines, agents and evaluation systems. Teams also call it an LLM engineer interview. The interview loop often includes a technical screen, a build round or take-home project, and an AI system design round.
No. An AI interview usually means an interview that AI software conducts. In an AI engineer interview, your engineers interview a candidate for an AI engineering role. Codility Interview has no AI interviewer, and your interviewers decide who advances.
Give the candidate a bounded build task, such as a RAG pipeline that answers questions about a set of documents and returns its sources. Before the session, agree on the scoring criteria with your interviewers. During the build, ask the candidate how they would handle malformed model output and how they would evaluate answer quality. In Codility Interview, the build and the system design discussion can run in the same session.
Codility’s AI-native task library includes a RAG task called Legal Document Q&A Assistant. Your engineers can also create custom Interview tasks with the Codility MCP connector. Ask each vendor to demonstrate a task and scoring rubric that match the AI engineering role you are hiring for.
Yes. Your team enables or disables the AI Assistant per assessment, and every candidate interaction with it is captured as reviewable AI activity. For interviews about how engineers build with AI coding tools, see vibe coding interviews.
Yes. Codility Interview runs technical interviews for software engineering and AI engineering roles, and your team picks the task for each role.
